absent: Locking, concurrency and memory ordering for topology, frequency and pressure data are not shown.
Population, initialization and update timing for cpu_topology, capacity, pressure and scale callbacks are absent.
Full APM device constants, apm_info layout and BIOS call effects beyond the selector are not shown.
Conduit discovery, trap implementation, quirk preservation details and extended register usage are absent.
Hypervisor side effects for KVM sharing, MMIO guard, time sync, paravirtual time and true random are not specified.
Error handling beyond return codes, argument validation and version negotiation state machines are absent.

findings.text: Three small per CPU accessors named topology_get_freq_ref and topology_get_freq_scale and topology_get_hw_pressure expose frequency reference and frequency scale and hardware pressure for a given CPU index. Each accepts a CPU number and returns an unsigned long from per CPU storage, with no locking or failure handling visible in the fragments.

Frequency scale origin is an enumeration with SCALE_FREQ_SOURCE_CPUFREQ first at zero followed by SCALE_FREQ_SOURCE_ARCH then SCALE_FREQ_SOURCE_CPPC then SCALE_FREQ_SOURCE_VIRT. A descriptor named scale_freq_data pairs a field named source holding one such origin with a callback named set_freq_scale that refreshes the scale with no arguments or result.

One logical CPU topology record named cpu_topology holds integer fields named package_id and cluster_id and core_id and thread_id together with CPU masks named llc_sibling and cluster_sibling and core_sibling and thread_sibling describing sharing at each hierarchy level.

Package and cluster and core identifiers plus pointers to core and thread and cluster and last level cache masks are obtained by indexing the global cpu_topology array with the CPU number. Thread detection named topology_core_has_smt has two builds, one reporting threaded when thread_id differs from minus one and another always reporting unthreaded, while arch_cpu_is_threaded constantly reports false.
The selector named APM_DEVICE_BALL picks APM_DEVICE_ALL when new and APM_DEVICE_OLD_ALL otherwise, keyed on whether apm_info connection_version exceeds code 0x0100 for release one point zero.

Variadic counting named COUNT_ARGS supports up to fifteen arguments with zero for empty input, built by shifting caller arguments through a fixed descending sequence in __COUNT_ARGS. Token joining named CONCATENATE expands arguments before pasting in __CONCAT.

Call identifiers pack type at bit thirty one and convention at bit thirty and owner at bits twenty nine through twenty four and function in the low sixteen bits. Standard uses zero and fast uses one and thirty two bit convention uses zero and sixty four bit uses one, with owner mask 0x3F and function mask 0xFFFF plus tests for fast and sixty four bit and extractors for owner and function and a composer named ARM_SMCCC_CALL_VAL from four parts.

Owner numbers assign zero to arch and one to CPU and two to SIP and three to OEM and four to standard and five to standard hypervisor and six to vendor hypervisor, with trusted application spanning forty eight to forty nine and trusted operating system spanning fifty to sixty three. Interface versions run from 0x10000 through 0x10003 for releases one point zero through one point three, quirks define none as zero and QCOM A6 as one, UID query uses 0xff01, and standard fast thirty two bit calls reserve zero for version and one for features and two for SOC identity plus 0x8000 and 0x7fff and 0x3fff for three workarounds and 0x10 for a CPU workaround, with SVE hint 0x10000 gathered into combined hints.

KVM vendor functions number features as zero and time sync as one and hypervisor memory info as two and memory share as three and memory unshare as four, with five and six reserved and seven for MMIO guard and eight through sixty three reserved and sixty four for version discovery and sixty five for CPU discovery and one hundred twenty seven for extended features, for a total of one hundred twenty eight. Composed fast identifiers use thirty two bit convention for features and time sync and UID query and sixty four bit convention for memory info and share and unshare and MMIO guard and both discovery calls under the vendor hypervisor owner, with a fixed vendor UUID for KVM.

Time sync selects virtual counter zero versus physical counter one. Paravirtual time under standard hypervisor sixty four bit fast calls uses 0x20 for features and 0x21 for stolen time. True random under standard fast calls uses 0x50 for version and 0x51 for features and 0x52 for UUID and 0x53 for random, with a sixty four bit variant sharing 0x53. Returns are zero for success and minus one for not supported and minus two for not required and minus three for invalid parameter, unaffected workaround return is one, and conduit order is none then SMC then HVC.

The short result named arm_smccc_res holds four unsigned slots from a0 through a3. The extended block named arm_smccc_1_2_regs holds eighteen unsigned slots from a0 through a17. The quirk descriptor named arm_smccc_quirk holds integer id plus a shared variant carrying only unsigned a6.

Converters named smccc_res_to_uuid and smccc_uuid_to_reg translate between a four word result and a sixteen byte UUID using little endian byte order within each word, mapping words in order to successive byte quartets and rebuilding one selected word from its quartet.

Generic SMC and HVC helpers accept up to eight input words plus optional result and quirk pointers, with convenience forms supplying a null quirk. Version one point one SMC and HVC forms forward a variable argument list and result pointer to a shared implementation, while a dispatcher queries the active conduit and invokes the matching form or otherwise records not supported and reports no conduit, returning the conduit actually used.

Inline register binding assumes an ARM thirty two bit register file with fixed r0 through r7 placement and distinct trap mnemonics per build, and the generic fallback produces an empty result without trapping. Callers must not rely on trap behavior elsewhere, must handle not supported when no conduit exists, and must preserve quirk state where required.
Per CPU storage access used by the topology getters is owned elsewhere and not specified here.
Each header defines a unique include guard macro to prevent multiple inclusion.
